key_insight: MICViT improves multimodal 3D brain MRI learning by separately modeling modality-specific and cross-modal context at both local and global scales.
clinical_relevance: This approach may support more accurate analysis of heterogeneous MRI datasets, such as brain age estimation, where combining complementary modalities can improve performance.
method: Four attention blocks: local/global intra-modal + local/global cross-modal
Designed for co-registered brain MRI modalities like T1, FLAIR, DWI, and SWI
evidence_signal: Evaluated on brain age prediction across three datasets—UK Biobank (n=41,404), SOOP (n=1,062), and Cam-CAN (n=613)—and outperformed CNN and transformer baselines, with larger gains as more modalities were added.
watch_item: Performance is shown on brain age prediction, so broader clinical generalization across tasks, scanners, and sites still needs validation.
paper_title: Modeling Local, Global, and Cross-Modal Context in Multimodal 3D MRI
